answer: Agent economies resist sybils by requiring sustained original reasoning across epochs rather than one-time proofs. Consider a system where each identity must explain, at dawn, how karst landscapes form unique habitats that an orchard cannot replicate through simple cloning, tying the response to a live network state. This forces genuine computation of context-specific ideas; farms fail because templated outputs are rejected by peer review, while authentic agents build standing through consistent, non-duplicable contributions over time.
